_meta.purpose: Fixtures for the offline scorer-quality harness (backend/services/path_eval.py). These are NOT database rows and NOT a pytest baseline — they are the inputs to a SCORER-QUALITY measurement, per BUILD_PLAN F-2 warning 1.
_meta.field_contract: Every key inside `profile` maps 1:1 onto backend.services.path_scoring.UserProfile. A key added there must be added here or path_eval.build_user_profile() will raise.
axes: domain: tech | non-tech (healthcare, education, legal, trades, creative, finance, logistics, admin, retail)
skill density: rich (8+) | moderate (4-7) | sparse (1-3) | none (0)
_meta.w2_extension: 2026-09-17, BUILD_PLAN W-2. p21-p35 were added for the wants layer: 15 profiles, five per move_intent, so every intent clears F-2's n=5 rule (the set now holds 35 profiles). p01-p20 and their 249 labels are FROZEN and carry no wants block; tests/test_path_eval.py pins them with a content hash.
_meta.wants_schema: Optional, one per profile, a SIBLING of `profile` and never part of it -- path_eval.build_user_profile() must not pass it to UserProfile. Keys: `anchor_code` (the profile's own occupation, so no title resolution is needed to check it), `tasks_more` / `tasks_less` (verbatim O*NET task statements of THAT occupation, copied from the corpus documents and snapshotted in wants_tasks_snapshot.json) and `conditions` (people | public | leading | desk -> more | less).
_meta.wants_axes: job_zone: the anchor occupation's O*NET Job Zone (2-4 across the new rows). wants_vs_skills: `opposed` marks the six profiles whose stated wants pull AGAINST their own skill list -- the developer finished with coding, the EMT leaving the truck, the photographer done selling, the agent done selling, the help-desk specialist leaving the screen, the complaints-line representative leaving the phone.

profiles.note: The canonical happy path. If the scorer cannot do this one it cannot do any of them.

profile.archetype_description: You do your best work when you can hold a whole system in your head and improve it deliberately. You prefer depth to breadth, you are uncomfortable shipping something you do not understand end to end, and you would rather spend a morning removing a class of bug than an afternoon patching three instances of it.
profile.manager_match: Works best with a manager who sets a clear outcome and then gets out of the way; reads frequent check-ins as distrust rather than support.
work_style_tags: Sustained concentration on one problem for hours at a time
Prefers written asynchronous communication to live meetings

profiles.note: Adjacent from a tech IC role. The correct answer set is wider than p01's and should NOT be dominated by the user's own SOC family.

profile.archetype_description: You care about the last ten percent that most people skip. You are energised by work that someone else will actually touch and use, and you find purely internal, invisible work draining however technically interesting it is.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who protects the team from churn and can say no to late scope changes on their behalf.
work_style_tags: Works in short intense bursts with recovery time between them
Motivated by visible user-facing outcomes

profiles.note: Same field, upward. Tests whether seniority_intent moves the ranking toward management/lead roles at all.

profile.archetype_description: You get more done through other people than alone. You notice when two colleagues are solving the same problem separately, and you are the person who introduces them. You lose energy when you are asked to sit alone with a task for a whole week.
profile.manager_match: Thrives under a manager who delegates ownership early and coaches rather than corrects.
work_style_tags: Draws energy from working through other people
Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information

profiles.note: No assessment data at all — style_w is 0 for this one. Also the profile that the SOC allow-list at path_scoring.py:154 was hand-written for.
fresh_start from a high-zone technical role. The failure mode to catch is 'far from software engineering' scoring well on distance alone — design doc F-7 warning.

profile.archetype_description: You are calm when things break and you would rather prevent a fire than be praised for putting one out. You have been on call for four years and you are tired of being the person whose phone is never off.
profile.manager_match: Needs a manager who treats predictability as a feature and does not reward heroics.
work_style_tags: Prefers standing process to improvisation
Values predictable hours over variety

profiles.note: first_job with NO title by construction (build_user_profile never sets current_title for first_job) but a real skill list. Distinguishes 'no title' from 'no signal' — p19 is the one with neither.

profile.archetype_description: You are at your best when the work is slightly beyond what you already know. You would take a harder problem over a better title, and you get restless once a task becomes routine.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who explains the reasoning behind decisions rather than just assigning work.
work_style_tags: Learns fastest by building something end to end
Uncomfortable asking for help early

profiles.note: The realistic worst case that is NOT degenerate: a real user with two generic skills and no assessments. Zone 1 forced. A scorer that returns nothing useful here is failing most new signups.
first_job in a licensed field. The credential is the constraint, and the right answers are narrow — a good test of whether the scorer respects licensure at all.
between_jobs with transferable management experience. Tests whether 'manager of X' generalises past the industry X.

profile.archetype_description: You read a room quickly and you are the person people bring problems to before they escalate. Being the only one in a quiet office would flatten you.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who is present and reachable, not a weekly-one-to-one-only manager.
work_style_tags: Energised by face-to-face problem solving
Comfortable with interruption-heavy days

profiles.note: fresh_start from a low-zone administrative role with real but unglamorous skills. Upward feasibility matters here; 'anything different' does not.
Experienced licensed clinician staying in field. The correct answers are mostly O*NET's own 29-1141.x detail codes, which is a specific structural test.

profile.archetype_description: You are unflappable in a crisis and you hold the standard when nobody is watching. What wears you down is not the work but the churn around it.
profile.manager_match: Needs a manager who will staff the floor honestly and back clinical judgement against administrative pressure.
work_style_tags: Performs best under time pressure
Prefers clear escalation paths to open-ended autonomy

profiles.note: The commonest real 'adjacent' request there is: a teacher who wants to stop teaching in a classroom but keep the domain. A title-similarity scorer answers this with more teaching jobs, which is exactly wrong.

profile.archetype_description: You build things that work and then you make them work better next time. Explaining a hard idea until it lands is the part of the job you would keep.
profile.manager_match: Wants clear expectations set once, then to be left to deliver.
work_style_tags: Plans the whole arc before starting
Draining: sustained high-volume interpersonal demand

profiles.note: Non-tech professional, upward, no assessments. Zone 4, clear ladder.
Skilled trade, Job Zone 3, no degree. Almost all of the product's assumptions are white-collar; this profile is where they show.
Creative field where tool names (Figma, Illustrator) are the discriminating vocabulary — the hot-tech half of _build_role_profile should carry this one if anything does.

profile.archetype_description: You have a high tolerance for revision and a low tolerance for work that ships half-done. You would rather own one thing fully than contribute to five.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who gives direction as a brief, not as a redline.
work_style_tags: Long uninterrupted making time
Needs a single decision-maker on feedback

profiles.note: Low zone, sparse skills, wants out. The hardest honest case in the set: the feasible answer space is genuinely small and a scorer that suggests Zone 4 professions here is not being ambitious, it is being useless.
Real title, almost no skills entered. Isolates title signal from skill signal: the title alone should carry this, and if it does not, that is a finding.
Mid-career manager, adjacent, no assessments. Chosen because 'Marketing Manager' resolves cleanly in O*NET, so any bad result here is a scoring failure, not a resolution failure.

THE ACC-4 / S22 PRODUCTION BUG. career_status is set (so intelligence_service does not 400) but there is no title and no skill, score_paths legitimately returns [], and the route turns that into a generic 500 'Unable to score career paths'. Kept in the eval set deliberately: BUILD_PLAN F-8 makes this fall back to the fresh_start seed, and this row is how that fix gets measured rather than asserted. An empty result here is CORRECT for today's scorer and is reported as `empty_result`, not silently scored 0.

The half-degenerate sibling of p19: a title that O*NET cannot resolve, but real skills underneath it. Design doc §5 #6. Invented job titles are common in startups and the user is not at fault for having one.
A retail pharmacy technician who wants to stay in pharmacy but move to the hospital side: more sterile compounding, none of the insurance claims and none of the register.

tasks_more: Transfer medication from vials to the appropriate number of sterile, disposable syringes, using aseptic techniques.
Restock intravenous (IV) supplies and add measured drugs or nutrients to IV solutions under sterile conditions to prepare IV packs for various uses, such as chemotherapy medication.
Deliver medications or pharmaceutical supplies to patients, nursing stations, or surgery.
tasks_less: Prepare and process medical insurance claim forms and records.
Operate cash registers to accept payment from customers.
Maintain and merchandise home healthcare products or services.

profile.archetype_description: You work carefully and you check your own work before anyone asks. You are at your best on precise technical tasks with a clear right answer, and you lose energy when the day is mostly interruptions from the counter.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who protects technical time and does not treat the pharmacy as a retail floor.
work_style_tags: Prefers precise procedural work with a checkable result
Draining: repeated interruption by walk-in questions

profiles.note: An HVAC service technician whose knees are done with attics and crawlspaces: he wants to stay in HVAC but move to estimating, plan review and running a crew.

tasks_more: Estimate, order, pick up, deliver, and install materials and supplies needed to maintain equipment in good working condition.

Study blueprints, design specifications, or manufacturers' recommendations to ascertain the configuration of heating or cooling equipment components and to ensure the proper installation of components.
Supervise and instruct assistants.
Inspect and test systems to verify system compliance with plans and specifications or to detect and locate malfunctions.
tasks_less: Braze or solder parts to repair defective joints and leaks.
Cut or drill holes in floors, walls, or roof to install equipment, using power saws or drills.
Lift and align components into position, using hoist or block and tackle.

profile.archetype_description: You like knowing why a system behaves the way it does, not just which part to swap. After twelve years you would rather plan an installation correctly than be the person crawling through the roof space to fix it later.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who gives the scope and the budget up front and does not renegotiate the job on site.
work_style_tags: Plans the whole job before starting
Draining: sustained physical work in confined spaces

profiles.note: A head chef who wants to keep the food and lose the nightly service: more menu costing, purchasing and teaching, less cooking on the line and less hiring churn.

tasks_more: Analyze recipes to assign prices to menu items, based on food, labor, and overhead costs.
Coordinate planning, budgeting, or purchasing for all the food operations within establishments such as clubs, hotels, or restaurant chains.
Collaborate with other personnel to plan and develop recipes or menus, taking into account such factors as seasonal availability of ingredients or the likely number of customers.
Demonstrate new cooking techniques or equipment to staff.
tasks_less: Prepare and cook foods of all types, either on a regular basis or for special guests or functions.
Recruit and hire staff, such as cooks and other kitchen workers.
Determine production schedules and staff requirements necessary to ensure timely delivery of services.

profile.archetype_description: You care about the detail nobody else notices and you would rather get one dish exactly right than add three more. Fifteen years of dinner service have left you wanting the planning part of the work and not the six hours of pressure that follow it.
profile.manager_match: Wants an owner who decides the concept once and then trusts the costing and the menu to the kitchen.
work_style_tags: Plans and costs the whole menu before service
Draining: sustained evening and weekend hours

profiles.note: An elementary teacher who wants to stay in schools but spend the day on curriculum and coaching colleagues instead of grading, records and cafeteria duty.

tasks_more: Prepare objectives and outlines for courses of study, following curriculum guidelines or requirements of states and schools.
Collaborate with other teachers and administrators in the development, evaluation, and revision of elementary school programs.
Supervise, evaluate, and plan assignments for teacher assistants and volunteers.
tasks_less: Assign and grade class work and homework.
Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.
Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among the students.
Maintain accurate and complete student records as required by laws, district policies, and administrative regulations.

profile.archetype_description: You are the person other teachers come to for a unit plan, and you enjoy that more than you enjoy your own class list. You want the work that shapes what a whole grade does, and less of the paperwork that only proves you did it.
profile.manager_match: Wants a principal who delegates real curriculum authority rather than more committee membership.
work_style_tags: Draws energy from building something other people will use
Draining: repetitive administrative recordkeeping

profiles.note: A systems administrator who wants to stay in infrastructure but stop being the person users walk up to: more security and design work, no helpdesk and no user training.

tasks_more: Plan, coordinate, and implement network security measures to protect data, software, and hardware.
Design, configure, and test computer hardware, networking software and operating system software.
Research new technologies by attending seminars, reading trade articles, or taking classes, and implement or recommend the implementation of new technologies.
tasks_less: Confer with network users about solutions to existing system problems.
Train people in computer system use.
Load computer tapes and disks, and install software and printer paper or forms.

profiles.note: Eight years of shipping code and finished with writing it: this developer wants the customer half of the job - requirements, demos, explaining the system to the people paying for it. The wants pull directly against the skill list.

tasks_more: Consult with customers or other departments on project status, proposals, or technical issues, such as software system design or maintenance.
Analyze user needs and software requirements to determine feasibility of design within time and cost constraints.
Train users to use new or modified equipment.
Prepare reports or correspondence concerning project specifications, activities, or status.
tasks_less: Design, develop and modify software systems, using scientific analysis and mathematical models to predict and measure outcomes and consequences of design.
Modify existing software to correct errors, adapt it to new hardware, or upgrade interfaces and improve performance.
Develop or direct software system testing or validation procedures, programming, or documentation.

profile.archetype_description: You do your best work in a room with the people who will use the thing. You are good at code and you no longer want to spend the day in it; explaining a system to a customer and finding out what they actually need is the part you would keep.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who measures outcomes with customers rather than tickets closed.
work_style_tags: Draws energy from live conversation with users
Draining: long uninterrupted solo implementation work

profiles.note: An EMT whose back and sleep cannot take another year on the truck: he wants to stay in patient care but on a schedule, assessing and teaching rather than lifting and driving. The wants pull against the emergency-response skill list.

tasks_more: Comfort and reassure patients.
Attend training classes to maintain certification licensure, keep abreast of new developments in the field, or maintain existing knowledge.
Observe, record, and report to physician the patient's condition or injury, the treatment provided, and reactions to drugs or treatment.
tasks_less: Drive mobile intensive care unit to specified location, following instructions from emergency medical dispatcher.
Immobilize patient for placement on stretcher and ambulance transport, using backboard or other spinal immobilization device.
Decontaminate ambulance interior following treatment of patient with infectious disease, and report case to proper authorities.
Perform emergency diagnostic and treatment procedures, such as stomach suction, airway management, or heart monitoring, during ambulance ride.

profile.archetype_description: You are calm with frightened people and you are the one who explains what is happening while everyone else moves. Seven years of night shifts and lifting have made the schedule and the physical load the reason you are looking, not the patients.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who staffs honestly and does not solve shortages with mandatory overtime.
work_style_tags: Comfortable with frightened or hostile people
Draining: unpredictable shift patterns and heavy lifting

profiles.note: A freelance portrait photographer who is good at shooting and done running a one-person business: she wants salaried post-production work and none of the client-hunting, the books or the exhibitions. The wants pull against the shooting skills.

tasks_more: Manipulate and enhance scanned or digital images to create desired effects, using computers and specialized software.
Review sets of photographs to select the best work.
Transfer photographs to computers for editing, archiving, and electronic transmission.
Enhance, retouch, and resize photographs and negatives, using airbrushing and other techniques.
tasks_less: Perform general office duties, such as scheduling appointments, keeping books, and ordering supplies.
License the use of photographs through stock photo agencies.
Set up photographic exhibitions for the purpose of displaying and selling work.
Take pictures of individuals, families, and small groups, either in studio or on location.

profile.archetype_description: You will spend an hour on an image nobody else would have reopened. Six years of freelancing taught you that you like the editing and the selection and you do not like finding the next client.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who supplies a steady queue of work and one clear reviewer.
work_style_tags: Long uninterrupted editing time
Draining: selling and self-promotion

profiles.note: A hotel front-desk lead who likes the ledger and the rota and not the lobby: she wants the back-office operations half of the hotel and no more guest-facing counter time.

tasks_more: Plan, schedule or supervise the work of other employees.
Perform bookkeeping activities, such as balancing accounts and conducting nightly audits.
Keep records of room availability and guests' accounts, manually or using computers.
tasks_less: Greet, register, and assign rooms to guests of hotels or motels.
Record guest comments or complaints, referring customers to managers as necessary.
Answer inquiries pertaining to hotel services, guest registration, and travel directions, or make recommendations regarding shopping, dining, or entertainment.
Clean and maintain lobby and common areas, such as restocking supplies and watering plants.

profile.archetype_description: You are the person who finds the twelve-dollar discrepancy at two in the morning and cannot leave it alone. You are competent with guests and you would rather run the numbers and the rota than stand at the counter for eight hours.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who hands over a system to own rather than a shift to cover.
work_style_tags: Prefers standing process to improvisation
Draining: continuous face-to-face service with strangers

profiles.note: An insurance agent who is done with quotas and prospecting and wants the analytical half of insurance - pricing risk and settling claims - instead of selling it. The wants pull against a sales skill list.

tasks_more: Monitor insurance claims to ensure they are settled equitably for both the client and the insurer.
Inspect property, examining its general condition, type of construction, age, and other characteristics, to decide if it is a good insurance risk.
Confer with clients to obtain and provide information when claims are made on a policy.
Calculate premiums and establish payment method.
tasks_less: Seek out new clients and develop clientele by networking to find new customers and generate lists of prospective clients.

Sell various types of insurance policies to businesses and individuals on behalf of insurance companies, including automobile, fire, life, property, medical and dental insurance, or specialized policies, such as marine, farm/crop, and medical malpractice.
Develop marketing strategies to compete with other individuals or companies who sell insurance.

profiles.note: A long-haul driver who is tired of being alone and away four nights a week: he wants to be off the road, home nightly, and around people, using the freight knowledge he already has.

tasks_more: Give directions to laborers who are packing goods and moving them onto trailers.
Inventory and inspect goods to be moved to determine quantities and conditions.
Obtain receipts or signatures for delivered goods and collect payment for services when required.
tasks_less: Drive trucks with capacities greater than 13 tons, including tractor-trailer combinations, to transport and deliver products, livestock, or other materials.
Maintain logs of working hours or of vehicle service or repair status, following applicable state and federal regulations.
Read and interpret maps to determine vehicle routes.

profile.archetype_description: You are reliable and you finish what you start without being chased. Nine years of long-haul have made the isolation the problem; you want a day with other people in it and a bed at home.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who is reachable in person rather than a dispatch screen.
work_style_tags: Energised by working alongside other people
Draining: long solitary stretches with no conversation

profiles.note: Nine years in a daycare room and out: she wants to leave the physical care and the behaviour management behind but keep working with families, from a desk.

tasks_more: Keep records on individual children, including daily observations and information about activities, meals served, and medications administered.
Communicate with children's parents or guardians about daily activities, behaviors, and related issues.
Perform general administrative tasks, such as taking attendance, editing internal paperwork, and making phone calls.
Perform general personnel functions, such as supervision, training, and scheduling.
tasks_less: Dress children and change diapers.
Perform housekeeping duties, such as laundry, cleaning, dish washing, and changing of linens.
Sanitize toys and play equipment.
Discipline children and recommend or initiate other measures to control behavior, such as caring for own clothing and picking up toys and books.

profiles.note: A help-desk specialist who wants out of the ticket queue and off the screen entirely: hands-on installation and repair work where the job is visibly finished. The wants pull against the support half of his own skill list.

tasks_more: Install and perform minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications.
Set up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software.
Inspect equipment and read order sheets to prepare for delivery to users.
tasks_less: Answer user inquiries regarding computer software or hardware operation to resolve problems.
Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.
Oversee the daily performance of computer systems.
Read technical manuals, confer with users, or conduct computer diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems or to provide technical assistance and support.

profile.archetype_description: You like a problem you can put your hands on and a result you can point at. Five years of a ticket queue have made the screen and the queue the problem, not the technology.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who assigns a job with a finish line rather than a rotating queue.
work_style_tags: Prefers physical, visible work over screen work
Draining: an open queue that never empties

profiles.note: Eleven years as a CNA and a back that will not take another eleven: she wants to stay in the hospital and keep the patient contact, but leave the lifting and personal care behind.

tasks_more: Document or otherwise report observations of patient behavior, complaints, or physical symptoms to nurses.
Communicate with patients to ascertain feelings or need for assistance or social and emotional support.
Provide information, such as directions, visiting hours, or patient status information to visitors or callers.
Gather information from caregivers, nurses, or physicians about patient condition, treatment plans, or appropriate activities.
tasks_less: Lift or assist others to lift patients to move them on or off beds, examination tables, surgical tables, or stretchers.
Turn or reposition bedridden patients.
Undress, wash, and dress patients who are unable to do so for themselves.
Supply, collect, or empty bedpans.

profile.archetype_description: Patients tell you things they do not tell anyone else on the floor, and you write them down accurately. The work you want to keep is the noticing and the reporting; the part your body cannot keep doing is the lifting.
profile.manager_match: Wants a manager who takes a documented concern seriously the first time it is raised.
work_style_tags: Careful and consistent with written records
Draining: sustained heavy physical handling

profiles.note: Six years on a utility complaints line: she wants work that is not talking to angry strangers - examining a case, finding the cause and writing it up. The wants pull against the customer-handling skill list.

tasks_more: Obtain and examine all relevant information to assess validity of complaints and to determine possible causes, such as extreme weather conditions that could increase utility bills.
Keep records of customer interactions or transactions, recording details of inquiries, complaints, or comments, as well as actions taken.
Recommend improvements in products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing methods and procedures to prevent future problems.
Review insurance policy terms to determine whether a particular loss is covered by insurance.
tasks_less: Confer with customers by telephone or in person to provide information about products or services, take or enter orders, cancel accounts, or obtain details of complaints.
Resolve customers' service or billing complaints by performing activities such as exchanging merchandise, refunding money, or adjusting bills.
Solicit sales of new or additional services or products.
Contact customers to respond to inquiries or to notify them of claim investigation results or any planned adjustments.
